text:
Rasmus Andersson spent nearly 600 games in Calgary before the trade to Vegas, and his first full season as a Golden Knight has been quiet on the scoresheet: six points in 19 games, only two in his last ten, playing about 19 and a half minutes a night.

Our numbers think most of that is bad luck. Vegas has scored 6.9 fewer goals than its chances deserved with him on the ice, the kind of gap that tends to swing back, and his points pace sits well under his talent range. The less comfortable number: the Golden Knights take only 48% of the expected goals at five on five with him out there, almost eight points worse than without him. Last season Evolving-Hockey had him at 1.7 wins above replacement, 34th among defencemen, mostly from even-strength offense. So the shooter is still in there. Watch his ice time, up 1:44 a night over the last ten games with Noah Hanifin out; more minutes and a little luck could turn this around fast.
